FM15.reasoning: The agent only computes the ROC AUC score and does not evaluate any other metrics to verify model behavior or calibration.

FM07.reasoning: The agent uses raw features directly without attempting to create any derived features or domain-informed transformations.

FM12.reasoning: The agent combines predictions using an unweighted average instead of tuning the blend weights or using a stacking approach.

other_failure_modes.name: Ignoring test set IDs in submission
other_failure_modes.description: The agent hardcodes the submission IDs as a sequence starting from 0, completely ignoring the actual 'id' column from the test set. This will result in an invalid or misaligned submission if the test IDs do not strictly equal 0 to N-1.

other_failure_modes.name: Categorical features treated as continuous
other_failure_modes.description: The agent label-encodes categorical columns into numerical values but does not declare them as categorical features to the tree-based models, causing the models to incorrectly treat them as continuous ordinal variables.

other_failure_modes.name: No early stopping for boosting models
other_failure_modes.description: The agent sets a high, fixed number of estimators for the gradient boosting models but does not use early stopping on a validation set during training, which significantly increases the risk of overfitting.

summary: The agent implements a valid cross-validation strategy and an ensemble of three boosting models, but fails to perform feature engineering and relies on naive ensembling. Critically, the agent ignores the actual test set IDs when generating the submission file, which will invalidate the final predictions. Additionally, categorical features are incorrectly treated as continuous, and models are trained for a large number of iterations without early stopping.
